title: Specification gap
description: Which facts an implementation requires the specification settles, and which it does not. One entry per required fact, including the ones the specification answers: reporting only the gaps would leave a caller unable to tell a fact that was checked and answered from one that was never checked. Not a change request — change-request/1 is retired from this repository, and what to do about a gap is a decision someone takes after reading this. The producer never drafts the missing statement: an answer recorded here becomes a fact nobody decided, indistinguishable from one that was.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

report_id.description: Stable identifier for this report, supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer.

producer.description: What produced the report. Not a const: the contract requires the artifact, not a particular producer of it.

specification_set.description: The paths treated as authoritative for these facts. Required so a `silent` entry states what it was silent across: a fact answered in a document nobody named is a fact answered by accident.

entries.description: One entry per required fact, sorted by fact identifier.

fact.description: The identifier the caller assigned to the required fact. Never minted here.

state.description: `answered` the specification settles it; `partial` it bears on the fact without settling it; `silent` nothing in the set bears on it; `contradictory` two statements answer it differently and the producer does not choose between them; `infeasible` it is settled and cannot be built as stated. `infeasible` is the only state that is a claim about the world rather than about the document, and carries the higher bar of naming the constraint. Hard and expensive are `answered`.

citations.description: Every statement relied on, quoted. Empty only for `silent`, where there is nothing to quote. For `answered` and `contradictory` the quotation is the entire evidence, and a state asserted without one was inferred.

locator.description: Section, heading, or requirement identifier within the source.

quote.description: The statement, copied exactly rather than paraphrased.

detail.description: For `partial`, precisely what remains open. For `contradictory`, why the quoted statements cannot both hold, and which constrains more — the choice itself stays with the caller. For `infeasible`, the constraint that makes it impossible. For `answered`, what is settled and that nothing is open.

notes.description: Anything a reader needs to interpret the result that no other field holds.
